info.name: CCAR Forecasting API
info.description:
Happy-path and negative tests for the CCAR Forecasting POC through the API gateway.

**Run order:** use the Collection Runner on the whole collection (folders 01-11 in order, including 10b). Folder 01 registers a fresh user and stores the JWT; folder 11 deletes it again.

**Environment:** import `CCAR-Local.postman_environment.json` and select it.

**Every response** is also checked against the shared contract: `X-Correlation-Id` echoed, and every 4xx/5xx is RFC 9457 problem+json with `errorCode`, `correlationId` (equal to the header), `service` and `timestamp`.

**Folder 03** needs KDB+ with the BU_HIERARCHY and GEO_HIERARCHY tables. **Folders 10 and 10b** call ccar-forecasting-service (/ccar/v1) through the gateway and need the CCAR_FORECAST / CCAR_ACTUALS / CCAR_VARIANCE tables in KDB+. **Folder 08** only runs its checks when a dependency is stopped; otherwise its tests are skipped.

item.name: 08 Resilience - run with a dependency stopped
item.description: These requests check failure handling when a dependency is down. With everything healthy their tests are SKIPPED, not failed. To exercise them: stop KDB+ (or point kdb.host at a dead host), stop ccar-hierarchy-service, or stop ccar-user-service, then run the matching request. Hierarchies are cached, so once loaded they keep serving while KDB+ is down; only a load or reload hits KDB+.

request.description: Start ccar-hierarchy-service with KDB+ down. First call: 503 KDB_UNAVAILABLE; following calls within 30 s: 503 BU_HIERARCHY_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After (fail fast, KDB+ not hit).
